name: stress_scenarios
description: Stress Lab scenarios for a single deal (R11): macro, sector, obligor, collateral, rating and combined shocks, the transmission from shocks to the obligor's financials and rating, and the pass, amber and breach rules. The R5 stress table (stress.json) is separate and unchanged.

shock_keys.revenue_pct: Change in revenue (decimal; -0.2 = revenue falls 20%). A number, or {default, by_sector}.
shock_keys.ebitda_margin_bps: Change in EBITDA margin in basis points of revenue (negative = squeeze).
shock_keys.receivable_days: Extra receivable or work-in-progress days, funded with new short-term debt.
shock_keys.delay_months: Project delay: revenue deferred by the sector's project share x months / 12, and the delayed work carried as receivables.
shock_keys.customer_loss: The largest customer is lost: revenue falls by the sector's largest-customer share.
shock_keys.rate_bps: Change in the benchmark rate (SAIBOR / EIBOR) in bps: floating deal pricing and the obligor's existing debt.
shock_keys.collateral_pct: Change in collateral value (decimal). A number for every pledged item, or {type: change}.
shock_keys.notches: Rating downgrade in notches, on top of any downgrade implied by the stressed financials.
shock_keys.guarantee_unenforceable: The guarantee (and credit insurance) gives no protection: PD, LGD and risk weight fall back to the obligor.

fixed_cost_share.basis: Operating leverage: a revenue fall costs EBITDA at the EBITDA margin plus the share of revenue that is fixed cost (EBITDA change = revenue change x (EBITDA margin + fixed-cost share)). Shares are the Risk Models sector cost-structure assumptions.

largest_customer_share.basis: Sector concentration assumption for the largest customer's share of revenue where the proposal gives no customer split.

project_revenue_share.basis: Share of annual revenue tied to project milestones that a delay defers.

short_term_funding_spread_bps.basis: Working capital absorbed by longer receivable days is funded with short-term debt at the benchmark (FTP reference tenor) plus this spread, interest only.

rating_overlay.basis: Financial-stress rating overlay: one notch for each full band-width the stressed obligor's DSCR or Debt/EBITDA deteriorates from where it stands today (bands: DSCR 2.0, 1.5, 1.25, 1.1, 1.0, 0.8; Debt/EBITDA 3, 4, 5, 6, 8; linear inside a band; the larger of the two moves; never an upgrade; at most 8 notches; EBITDA at or below zero takes the maximum). The PD model has no financial-ratio features, so this overlay carries a financial shock into PD, rating and stage; the book's median DSCR falls and leverage rises from AA to C (corp_borrower_quarter 2026Q2).

stage_rules.basis: IFRS 9 SICR: Stage 2 when the stressed rating is at least the policy's SICR notches (pd_migration) below the rating at origination (today, for a new deal), or the stressed DSCR is below 1.0 (debt service not covered, a watch-list trigger); Stage 3 at CC or worse (unlikely to pay).

bands.basis: Pass, amber, breach: amber when a ratio is within 10% of its covenant or limit, or RAROC is within 2 points of the hurdle; breach when the limit, the covenant, DSCR 1.0, the hurdle or Stage 1 is lost.

breakeven_ranges.basis: Reverse stress searches each driver over this range; a failure not reached inside it is reported as 'beyond range'.

scenarios.label: Oil −30%
scenarios.basis: Brent 30% below the planning price for four quarters: government capex and petrochemical prices fall; revenue sensitivity by sector from the Risk Models GCC oil-transmission assumptions.

scenarios.label: SAIBOR / EIBOR +200 bps
scenarios.basis: A parallel 200 bps rise in the benchmark: floating deal pricing and the obligor's existing debt reprice; fixed-rate deals are match-funded.

scenarios.label: GDP −3%
scenarios.basis: Real non-oil GDP 3% below plan: revenue falls by the sector's GDP beta x 3% (beta 0.5 for utilities and healthcare to 3.0 for construction).

scenarios.label: Real estate prices −20%
scenarios.basis: Real estate values 20% down: pledged real estate is revalued; real estate rents and new construction starts fall.

scenarios.label: Construction downturn
scenarios.basis: Construction revenue −25% and receivable days +60 (delayed government and developer payments); suppliers to construction take the spill-over.

scenarios.label: Trading slowdown
scenarios.basis: Import and re-export volumes fall: trading revenue −15%, margin −100 bps, debtor days +30; logistics and manufacturers that sell through traders take the spill-over.

scenarios.label: Revenue −10%
scenarios.basis: Obligor revenue 10% below the latest audited year, with operating leverage.

scenarios.label: Revenue −20%
scenarios.basis: Obligor revenue 20% below the latest audited year, with operating leverage.

scenarios.label: Revenue −30%
scenarios.basis: Obligor revenue 30% below the latest audited year, with operating leverage.

scenarios.label: Largest customer lost
scenarios.basis: The largest customer stops buying: revenue falls by the sector's largest-customer share.

scenarios.label: Project delay 6 months
scenarios.basis: Milestone revenue slips 6 months; the work done is carried as receivables until certified.

scenarios.label: Project delay 12 months
scenarios.basis: Milestone revenue slips 12 months; the work done is carried as receivables until certified.

scenarios.label: EBITDA margin −300 bps
scenarios.basis: Input costs rise faster than prices: EBITDA margin 3 points lower on the same revenue.

scenarios.label: Collateral −20%
scenarios.basis: Every pledged item revalued 20% lower (forced-sale discount over the haircut).

scenarios.label: Collateral −30%
scenarios.basis: Every pledged item revalued 30% lower.

scenarios.label: Collateral −40%
scenarios.basis: Every pledged item revalued 40% lower (distressed market).

scenarios.label: Guarantee unenforceable
scenarios.basis: The guarantee or credit insurance cannot be called (open-ended wording, a defective legal opinion): the deal stands on the obligor alone.

scenarios.label: Rating −1 notch
scenarios.basis: One-notch downgrade: PD from the model at the lower grade.

scenarios.label: Rating −2 notches
scenarios.basis: Two-notch downgrade: PD from the model at the lower grade.

scenarios.label: Rating −3 notches
scenarios.basis: Three-notch downgrade, the policy's SICR threshold: PD from the model at the lower grade.

scenarios.label: Severe combined
scenarios.basis: Macro, sector and collateral together: oil −30%, rates +200 bps, the obligor's own sector downturn (GDP −3% where none is defined) and collateral −30%. Revenue changes compound; bps, days and notches add.
